summary.text: 得 means “obtain” or “get.” Early forms are interpreted as a hand taking a shell. In the received graph’s traditional analysis, 彳 contributes movement and 㝵 supplies a sound cue; the historical sound match is not confirmed.

formation.text: The received graph is analyzed as phonosemantic: 彳 contributes movement, while 㝵 is assigned a phonetic role. Early hand-and-shell forms offer a separate graphic explanation for “obtain.” The phonetic analysis is explicit in the Shuowen tradition, but no paired historical reconstruction verifies the sound match.

components.text: 彳 contributes movement in the traditional analysis of 得. Its relationship here to 行 is not established as a full-form relationship.

The Shuowen tradition assigns 㝵 a phonetic role in 得 and associates it with “take.” The graphs 㝵 and 䙷 are treated as variants in the historical lexicographic tradition. Later shapes resembling 目, 日, or 旦, and a seal form resembling 見, have also been described, but their relation to this component is unsettled.

sound_limitation.text: Modern Mandarin readings of 㝵 and 得 are both dé, but this pair does not establish their historical sound relationship. No component-specific historical reconstruction for 㝵/䙷 was verified; 得 is reconstructed as *tˤək in the Baxter–Sagart system and *tɯːɡ in the Zhengzhang system.

sound.text: Both graphs have the modern Standard Mandarin reading dé. This current reading pair is compatible with the traditional phonetic analysis but does not verify an ancient sound match.

history.text: Early forms are interpreted as a hand taking a shell. The curated oracle-style drawing represents this interpretation; it is a modern redraw, and the shell-like element does not establish the object’s original name or pronunciation.

Later forms are described as changing 又 to 寸 and reshaping 貝 toward forms resembling 目, 日, or 旦. A received seal form resembling 見 has been described as a possible corruption of 貝. The full sequence is not confirmed by a continuous series of dated forms.
The Shuowen tradition analyzes 得 as 彳 plus phonetic 㝵. Variant dictionaries connect 䙷 and 㝵 as old or alternative forms, without establishing the complete chronology of the graph’s shapes.

uncertainties.text: The earliest character-specific attestation and its date remain unresolved. The hand-and-shell account explains the proposed graphic meaning but does not establish the shell’s original name or pronunciation.
The relationship between the early hand-and-shell picture and the later 彳-plus-㝵 analysis, including when 㝵 took on its traditionally assigned phonetic role, remains unclear.
A reported comparison with Tibetan thub is unverified. The chronology of extended and grammatical uses is disputed.

senses.period: Dating unresolved; attested in Warring States manuscript examples
senses.text: The hand-taking-shell interpretation proposes “obtain” as the graph’s original sense, though its earliest secure attestation date is unresolved. Warring States manuscript examples use 得 to mean “obtain” or “get” by that period.

senses.gloss: meet, use, understand, finish, suffice, reach, be able; auxiliary and particle functions
senses.period: Historical; individual developments and dates unresolved
senses.text: These meanings and grammatical uses are recorded, but their order and development from “obtain” are not established. One study argues that pre-Qin examples still mean “obtain” and that auxiliary use had not yet developed; other descriptions place a possibility use earlier, leaving the chronology disputed.
Modern usage includes “obtain,” “get,” “gain,” and “acquire.” These meanings alone do not show when or how the other historical uses developed.

limitations.text: No dated sequence links “obtain” to the listed extended and grammatical uses, so no specific semantic transitions are asserted.
The reported relationship with Tibetan thub does not establish borrowing, cognacy, direction, or sound correspondences.
